Read-only second review (Opus). Not built here.

Verdict: Ready to merge.

Blockers: none.

What I read: the full diff of the three files, `chamfer_ride.rs` at this head (299 lines), its caller in `crates/app/src/operation/material_source.rs:223-229`, the issue #2887 and the two earlier reviews.

Checks:

- The refusal fires only on a matched top loop that has a segment more than `MATCH_SLACK` (0.05 mm) from the wall AND more than one chamfer width of segments within `SAME_EDGE` (1e-6 mm) of the wall. A fully sharp loop has no bevelled segment. A fully bevelled loop has no sharp segment. The two cases go to the old `match`, unchanged. The sharp test uses the same `SAME_EDGE` value as the old classification at `chamfer_ride.rs:85`, so no loop that was sharp before reads differently now.
- The per-segment sample (two ends and the middle) reads the reported plate as partly bevelled with and without the extra vertex. I checked the two cases by hand: the segment X1 Y0 to X1 Y40 has its middle 1 mm from the wall.
- The refusal is in `ride_loops`, in the region step of the source-built (no-pick) path. It returns before any toolpath exists. No partial path is possible. The text names a point on each part and tells the user what to do.
- A path that passed before cannot give a different toolpath: the new code only adds an early `Err`. When it does not fire, the old code runs on the same values.
- Index and float math: `top[(i + 1) % top.len()]` runs only inside the loop over `top`, so the length is not zero. `wall` is checked for empty. `hypot`, `max` and the thresholds are safe. A NaN distance falls into neither class and does not refuse.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` outside tests. No test is removed or made weaker.
- File sizes: `chamfer_ride.rs` 299 lines, the new test file 145 lines.
- Test placement: `crates/app/tests/chamfer_partly_bevelled.rs` uses app commands (`History`, `GenerateOperation`), so `crates/app/tests/` is correct. It has its Gate map line.
- The decision file follows the `docs/decisions/README.md` format. The `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #2887` are present. No byte-order mark in the new files.
- The finding of the first collaborator review (heavy lane results on the final head) is met: the PR body records them for this head. These are the author's results. This review did not run them.

Notes (not blockers):

1. `chamfer_ride.rs:138-160`: the check refuses any partial plan offset larger than 0.05 mm, not only a modelled chamfer. Example: a plate with a draft of more than about 3 degrees on one side and vertical walls on the other sides (1 mm width, 90-degree cone). Before this PR, such a loop rode its wall section, and that ride is a valid chamfer. Now it refuses, and the text says "modelled chamfer". The decision file says that no program that posted before is refused now. That is shown for a modelled bevel only. The refusal is the safe direction. I recommend a `P7` follow-up issue: a test with one drafted side, and a decision if that case must still ride.
2. The new app tests have no control case that still cuts. The seven older tests in `chamfer_modelled_edge` (#303, #2435, #2596) are the cutting controls, and the reviews report them green. The unit test `a_loop_bevelled_all_round_is_not_partly_bevelled` calls `partly_bevelled` only, not `ride_loops`.
3. The issue also asks for a note that names the edges that the operation leaves sharp. The PR body says that this is separate work, but it gives no issue number. Please file it as a tracked follow-up issue, so that the item is not lost.
